To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CON laws and Medicaid reimbursement policy are effective in restricting nursing home supply and access, respectively.

(1) about 2 percent to 11 percent of consumers who demand for a nursing home do not enter any nursing home; (2) about one fourth of all nursing homes face a binding bed-constraint; (3) the Medicaid payment rate is set at about 70 percent of the price of the first-choice nursing homes.

the CON laws have a significant effect on the number of nursing home beds and the number of Medicaid consumers who can enter their first-choice facilities; Medicaid consumers who are denied access to the nursing homes of their choice are not necessarily denied access to any nursing homes; the Medicaid payment rates have a significant effect not only on the prices charged to Medicaid consumers but also on the prices charged by the nursing homes that do not serve Medicaid consumers.
